questions.question: Explain what appropriate technology is and why it is important for small-scale farmers.
questions.expected_answer: Technology suited to social, economic and environmental conditions; Schumacher, Small is Beautiful 1973, intermediate technology. Features: affordable, simple to use/maintain/repair with local skills and materials, local resources and knowledge, small-scale and labour-intensive, environmentally sustainable. Not primitive: can include solar panels, mobile phones, drip kits, Hippo Water Roller (SA, early 1990s, about 90 L). High-tech inputs can be unaffordable, cause debt and harm. Important for small-scale/subsistence farmers and food gardens.

questions.question: Describe appropriate technologies for managing water in farming.
questions.expected_answer: Rainwater harvesting (roof gutters, tanks, underground tanks, contour banks/ridges); zaï planting pits (Yacouba Sawadogo, Burkina Faso; manure, termites, water infiltration); drip irrigation (emitters, less evaporation and runoff, about half the water of flood irrigation, gravity kits, bottle drip); grey water reuse; treadle pumps and solar pumps; mulching to reduce evaporation and weeds.

questions.question: Describe farming techniques that improve soil and control pests, and how they are used in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Composting, manure, trench beds; crop rotation (different nutrients, breaks pest cycles; legumes fix nitrogen via root nodule bacteria); intercropping (maize, beans, pumpkins; spreads risk); conservation agriculture; integrated pest management (predators, repellent plants, pesticides last resort); push-pull (desmodium repels stem borer moths and suppresses striga; Napier grass attracts and traps; fodder); agroforestry. SA: dual farming system; household, school (linked to NSNP), clinic, church and urban community gardens (Cape Flats, Soweto); indigenous crops (sorghum, millet, cowpeas, bambara groundnuts, amaranth/morogo/imifino) drought-tolerant and nutritious; community seed banks; post-harvest: airtight storage, solar dryers; mobile phone information. Limits: need land, water, training, credit, roads and markets.
